messages:
Anna Li: FYI I sketched a small follow-up to the safetensors loader RFC — proposing a 'segmented load' model where we split a shard into multiple TTL slabs (hot, warm, cold) and evict by-slab rather than whole-shard. intent: reduce OOM spike on model switches and allow prioritized warmup of critical layers
Mike Patel: can you paste the high-level flow?
Anna Li: sure — flow: 1) manifest exposes slab offsets + priority hint 2) loader asks weightstore for required slabs 3) weightstore maintains per-slab lease + credit counters 4) runtime uses priority to prefetch hot slabs first, warm slabs lazily, cold on demand
Rajiv Kumar: how do we define slabs? layer-boundaries? megabyte chunks?
Anna Li: good q. my current thought: prefer semantic boundaries (logical layer groups) when available in format; fallback to fixed byte-chunks for opaque safetensors. we annotate manifest with either "layer-slab" or "byte-slab" schema
Sophia Chen: hmm manifests grow more complex. backwards compat concerns?
Anna Li: backwards: loader accepts old manifest (single-slab) and maps it to a single hot-slab. new clients can opt-in. no mandatory on-disk change — manifests can be sidecar JSON if we want non-breaking
Mike Patel: eviction: if we evict slab B but keep A, does wiring for KV-cache need to change? we currently assume contiguous KV pages per shard
Rajiv Kumar: KV-cache granularity is the sticky part. we could keep KV at per-layer granularity which aligns with layer-slab. for byte-slabs we may need an overlay mapping from byte-range -> KV segments
Anna Li: exactly. proposal suggests runtime maintain a lightweight slab->kv mapping. fallback: if mapping missing, runtime falls back to conservative full eviction to preserve correctness
Sophia Chen: tradeoffs on metadata size + parsing perf? sidecar JSON for every checkpoint might bloat telemetry
Anna Li: we compress and canonicalize manifests; they live in registry with content-addressing. runtime caches parsed manifests and shares across workers. parsing cost is a one-time per-registry-entry hit
Mike Patel: what about warmup policies: how do we schedule prefetch across replicas to avoid thundering herd?
Anna Li: weightstore will expose a lease/token system. warmup coordinator issues soft leases; replicas with highest priority get first tokens. also jittered backoff and leader-election for in-region prefetching
Rajiv Kumar: sounds similar to our existing hotstart coordinator but with slab-awareness. is this a refactor or additive?
Anna Li: mostly refactor-ish. introduce slab metadata plumbing end-to-end. weightstore + coordinator changes are additive but runtime will get new eviction path — so both)
Sophia Chen: is safetensors format the only target? or do we push manifest changes across formats?
Anna Li: goal is format-agnostic manifest. safetensors gets early wins because we can map tensor names easily. For binary-only formats, sidecar manifests provide same API surface
Mike Patel: failure modes? partial slab fetch corrupted mid-warmup?
Anna Li: weightstore will publish checksums per-slab. loader will validate on fetch; failed slab fetch triggers rollback: either re-fetch or escalate to full-shard fallback path. telemetry will flag repeated slab corruption to registry
Rajiv Kumar: perf numbers needed. can we simulate a 30B model with highest-30% layers hot and measure tail P99 latency with and without slab eviction?
Anna Li: I can prototype a simulator next week — will try to include mem and io graphs.
Sophia Chen: API boundary ask: keep loader API as `request_slabs(shard_id, slab_ids)` and `release_slabs(lease_id)`?
Anna Li: yup, small and orthogonal. also `manifest_for_model(version)` to get slab map
infra-bot: deploybot: new design doc uploaded to google drive: https://drive.internal/reed/safeload-segmentation-draft — Anna Li is owner
Mike Patel: kudos. next steps: Anna + Rajiv prototype mapping and KV overlay, Sophia to validate manifest storage/caching cost, I'll look at coordinator token design
Anna Li: thanks all. I'll post the draft and a short TL;DR for eng-sre ops rollback considerations.
